stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula y = 7x.
Think first: x is multiplied by 7, so dividing by 7 will release it.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p095-q03 from workbook page 95.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by 7 and write x on the left.

whyThisWorks.value: 7x means 7 multiplied by x, and division is the inverse of multiplication. Dividing both sides by 7 cancels the 7 on the right and leaves x by itself, while the equal sign stays valid because both sides were divided by the same amount.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = 7y instead of y/7.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = y − 7, treating the 7 as if it were added.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = y − 7, treating the 7 as if it were added.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only the right-hand side by 7.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing only the right-hand side by 7.

examTip.value: Ask what is being done TO the subject, then do the opposite: multiplied means divide, added means subtract, squared means square root.
